item.title: Raiders' No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza will get 'plenty of experience' in preseason debut Thursday
item.description: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said that Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, will get "plenty of experience" as he's set for first preseason action.
item.content:encoded:
Preseason football are not always the most exciting games to watch, but Las Vegas Raiders fans will surely be tuned in Thursday night against the Arizona Cardinals.

Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick of the 2026 NFL Draft and the future at quarterback for the franchise, will take his first NFL snaps in a real game.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said that Mendoza will be getting "plenty of experience in the game," as he also prepares for his first time leading the Raiders on the sideline.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Kubiak, fresh off a Super Bowl victory with the Seattle Seahawks as their offensive coordinator, is looking to lead the Raiders back to playoff contenders in his first season. And though he named Kirk Cousins as their starting quarterback right now in training camp, Mendoza is someone he will need to develop into the franchise quarterback the organization believes he can be.

"Look forward to seeing him out there with his teammates," Kubiak said, according to Raiders.com. "Lot of guys that we need to evaluate but he'll get plenty of reps."

RAIDERS' FERNANDO MENDOZA SHARES TOM BRADY'S ADVICE AS HE BEGINS NFL CAREER

Cousins joined the team in free agency, and Kubiak always made it known that he preferred the veteran to lead the way first before Mendoza took over as the team’s starter.

That is the plan, but Mendoza will have a heavy spotlight on him during these preseason games to see how quickly he has learned Kubiak’s offense, as well as his chemistry with new teammates.

Starters are expected to play a couple series, though, which should mean Cousins is the first quarterback to step foot on the field for the Raiders. From there, Mendoza and Aidan O’Connell will take the reins at quarterback.

But just because Cousins has been named the starter, it doesn’t mean Kubiak can’t change his mind. Mendoza could play so well this preseason that Kubiak decides he is ready for regular-season NFL play.

Time will tell, but Mendoza’s expectations are through the roof and fans will be looking for him to execute quickly, even if the games don’t count toward their 2026 record just yet.

item.title: Hasan Piker cheers Mamdani aide going 'beast mode' with 'impoverish the White middle-class' remark
item.description: Hasan Piker called Cea Weaver "beast mode" after Bill Maher highlighted the Zohran Mamdani aide's comments about impoverishing the White middle class.
item.content:encoded:
The socialist Twitch streamer who claimed America "deserved 9/11" heaped praise on an aide to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani who previously professed hope of "impoverishing the White middle-class."

Hasan Piker was in the middle of a long riff mocking liberal comic Bill Maher over his incredulity at various socialist platforms on his "Real Time" program when he responded to Maher’s criticism of Mamdani aide Cea Weaver.

"Mamdani’s top aide, Cea Weaver said, ‘if you don't believe in the government's sacred right to seize property, it's over’, and ‘impoverish the White middle-class’," Maher said last week, before Piker interrupted the clip.

"You know you’re supposed to scare people into voting ‘for’ you, right," Maher quipped.

PIKER TELLS MAMDANI TO ‘SHUT THE F--- UP’ OVER CAUTIOUS MESSAGING, CLAIMS MAYOR NEEDS TO BE MORE 'BOLD'

Piker interjected that he "love[s Weaver] so much."

"Beast mode," he said. "One of the things I love about Zohran is that the people surrounding him are oftentimes are so much cooler than he is — but that's also part of the reason why I really respect what he's doing; she's awesome."

FLASHBACK: MAMDANI'S HISTORY OF DODGING QUESTIONS ABOUT WHERE HE STANDS ON KEY ISSUES

The phrase "beast mode," referencing total focus and brute power, was popularized in the 2010s by former Seattle Seahawks running back Marshawn Lynch in an apolitical context.

Weaver, who is White, grew up in a wealthy neighborhood of Rochester and attended the School of the Arts in the upstate city, according to a profile in the Rochester Democrat & Chronicle. Mamdani's predecessor, Eric Adams, said Weaver's comments exuded "extreme privilege and total detachment from reality."

Meanwhile, Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed called Piker’s 2019 comments about the 9/11 terror attacks "dumb" in a Sunday interview with NBC but remains an ally of the far-left streamer.

Piker, who has appeared with his uncle Cenk Uygur on the progressive "Young Turks" program, has also appeared with other far-left candidates and figures, including Rep. Summer Lee, D-Pa., and Wisconsin State Assemblywoman Francesca Hong, D-Maple Bluff, who narrowly lost the Democratic nomination for governor on Tuesday.

JD VANCE WARNS 'LIMOUSINE SOCIALISTS' WILL DESTROY MICHIGAN AUTO JOBS, DEPRESS AMERICAN WAGES

Piker continued his attacks on Maher, including for telling Vice President JD Vance his vote could be up for grabs in 2028 if Democrats align themselves with socialists.

At one point, Maher criticized Piker, saying the far-left’s "most popular influencer… thinks Communism is so groovy, he laments the fall of two of the most murderous regimes in history."

Piker responded by saying Maher’s ensuing mention of the USSR is a "bastardization of my quote" and disputed the comic's contention that the China of Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping has ever actually "fallen." Mao died in 1976, and Deng soon emerged as China's de facto leader, holding several official roles through 1990 before his death in 1997.

Piker disputed Maher's suggestion that the China of Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping had similarly "fallen." Mao died in 1976, after which Deng emerged as China's paramount leader and oversaw sweeping reforms through 1990.

MARK HALPERIN CALLS HASAN PIKER A 'HORRIBLE PERSON' AS DEMOCRATS FACE PRESSURE TO DISTANCE FROM STREAMER

"The fall of the USSR was one of the great catastrophes of the 20th century. Mao Zedong is one of the great leaders of this world. Both are true. Both are objectively true statements," Piker said, calling Maher "smug" and suggesting he "read a book."

Piker then defended his comments about the USSR by saying Russian President Vladimir Putin — "certainly no Communist" — agrees with him.

Putin, an ex-Soviet KGB agent, said in 2005 the 1991 collapse of the USSR was the "greatest geopolitical catastrophe" in history.

Fox News Digital reached out to Weaver through Mamdani’s office and to Maher through Warner Bros. Discovery for comment.

item.title: Paris Jackson says dad Michael’s unusual rule helped protect her childhood
item.description: Paris Jackson revealed on "Call Her Daddy" that Michael Jackson required his kids to finish homework and chores before enjoying Neverland attractions.
item.content:encoded:
Behind the glitz of Michael Jackson’s larger-than-life world, Paris Jackson said her father enforced a strict rule to protect his children’s sense of normalcy.

The late King of Pop kept a tight rein on his children despite their unusual upbringing. Jackson recalled her father requiring them to finish their homework and chores before earning weekend fun, limiting television and movies and having them wear masks in public to shield their identities from the intense spotlight surrounding his fame.

"The cool, like very congruent line throughout my childhood that kind of started there and then just continued on wherever we went was, if you're good, and you do your chores, and you do your homework, and you do the things that you're supposed to do. Then on the weekends you can go see some animals, and you can go ride some rides, and you can go to the movies," she told "Call Her Daddy" host Alexandra Cooper.

VICTORIA BECKHAM REVEALS STRICT NO-PHONES RULE AT FAMILY DINNER KEEPS HER KIDS GROUNDED

"It was made very, very clear that all of the attractions [at Neverland] were not for us," she added. "That it did not belong to us. That was for, you know, underprivileged children and children that were terminally ill that couldn't go to like Disneyland."

Paris said the rule remained in place as the family moved frequently and rarely stayed anywhere for more than a year.

"If we were living in Vegas, and it's like, 'OK, if you're good you can go to Circus Circus on the weekends.' Or like we were in like some random place in Virginia. Like, 'OK, if you're good you can go to Chuck E. Cheese this weekend,'" she recalled.

Michael’s rules extended to television. Paris said his children could watch movies or TV after completing their responsibilities, with an exception of studying film without sound.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Michael also took steps to protect his children from the spotlight, having them wear masks in public so they could go unnoticed.

"I mean it just, it made sense because it was like, 'Oh yeah, if you do this now, then you can go to Chuck E. Cheese and be normal this weekend 'cause no one will know who you are,'" the "Wilted" singer recalled. "Like that made sense to me."

The masks helped Paris maintain some anonymity, but she still understood that her father was famous. What she didn’t grasp was the sheer magnitude of his celebrity.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I just didn't know how famous ... There was definitely part of me that, like when I looked out my hotel window, and it was one of the times where like the alias didn't work and there's just like a sea of people with signs and stuff – I'm not so naive to think, yeah, everyone experiences this, you know?" Paris admitted. "I just didn't understand the lengths."

Jackson, the only daughter of late pop superstar and Debbie Rowe, built an entertainment career through modeling, acting and music.

After making highly publicized appearances with her family following Michael Jackson's 2009 death, she pursued modeling and landed acting roles before signing with Republic Records and releasing her debut album, Wilted, in 2020.

She has two brothers, Prince Jackson and Bigi Jackson.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham vs DiJonai Carrington: How two ex-football players collided in the 'privilege' debate
item.description: DiJonai Carrington and Sophie Cunningham's paths from football fields to the WNBA reveal how two players became symbols of the league's deepest divide.
item.content:encoded:
It was one dreaded moment after another for the WNBA.

Months of conflict came to a breaking point Saturday when DiJonai Carrington struck Sophie Cunningham in the face. A scuffle ensued, Carrington was ejected and then came the social media post that lit the internet on fire.

"White privilege."

DIJONAI CARRINGTON DECLARES 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' AFTER EJECTION FOR SMACKING SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM IN THE FACE

And just like that, the WNBA discourse was about race again. Not just sex, as it had been for weeks.

The hit was a product of two different players from two different worlds, but with novel similarities.

The WNBA's infamous hit just so happened to involve two former football players that played against boys.

Carrington played two years of flag football and then two years of tackle during her elementary school years. She wanted to play because her brother and sister played it too.

Growing up in San Diego, Carrington's father Darren Carrington played for five different NFL teams, but they called San Diego home.

Her father's career earnings are not known, but based on the averages of NFL salaries at the time, he likely made multiple millions of dollars across his eight-year career. DiJonai attended the private Horizon Christian Academy, where her mother was her basketball coach coach.

On the first day of 2015, DiJonai penned an essay that was published in ESPN.com about flying out to California to watch her brother, Darren Jr., play in the Rose Bowl.

Meanwhile, Cunningham went to public high school in Columbia, Missouri. But she attended a private Catholic school during her younger years.

Cunningham played football at Rock Bridge High School with grown boys, but didn't do any tackling like Carrington did in elementary school.

Cunningham was a placekicker, and was protected from any plays that involved tackling, but she still made school history as the first girl to score varsity points.

She grew up on a 2,500 acre farm, and once suggested she came from a "blue-collar" background.

"I would never speak down upon middle class, blue-collar working people. That's where I come from," Cunningham said last July, in an apology for criticizing the selection of Cleveland as a WNBA expansion city.

Her maternal family operated a large farm while her father worked as a building contractor, but things changed for the Cunningham family in 2008.

Cunningham revealed in a July interview on the "Sons and Daughters" podcast, that the 2008 financial crisis impacted her family.

"We were raised in a really good family who gave us more than what we could think of. But that doesn't mean that we didn't have hard times. Our dad was a contractor in the 2008 Economic [crisis], all that stuff that hit our family very hard. And when I say very hard, very very hard," she said.

"And so people look at me and it's really easy to be like 'Oh, she had everything' or 'She did whatever.' It's like, no, we went through some hard times as a family. But honestly, looking back, those were our most fun times. Like we were in a smaller house. We were together 24/7. There were no extra rooms to go to. Some people could be embarrassed by that, but I take great pride like 'Hey, our family isn't built on fluff and all the shiny and crazy things. We have a real family that when hard times hit, they're going to show you even more love than you knew existed."

Both were nationally ranked recruits. Both became McDonald's All-Americans. Both played AAU basketball, which put them in front of college coaches beyond their hometowns.

But Cunningham's recruitment was practically over before she entered high school.

After eighth grade, Cunningham joined the Missouri Eclipse on the AAU circuit. Missouri coach Robin Pingeton began recruiting both Sophie and her older sister Lindsey, eventually offering each a full scholarship.

The sisters committed to Missouri, even as Cunningham's reputation grew and other coaches continued calling.

The decision kept her close to home, but it also continued a family tradition. Her mother, father, aunt, uncle and grandfather had all competed for Missouri.

And Sophie immediately became the face of the program.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

In her fourth college game, she scored a school-record 42 points against Wake Forest. She was named SEC Freshman of the Year and helped Missouri reach the NCAA Tournament for the first time in a decade.

The Tigers made the tournament in all four of her seasons.

By the end of her career, Cunningham was a three-time First-Team All-SEC selection and a Third-Team All-American. She finished as Missouri's all-time leading scorer with 2,187 points and also set the school record for free throws made.

Carrington took a longer winding road through college.

Two ACL surgeries limited her to two and a half seasons of high school basketball. But she still scored more than 2,000 points, played for Cal Sparks Gold on the club circuit and became a five-star recruit.

She first committed to Stanford, the famed elite university on the West Coast.

Carrington came off the bench as a freshman for a team that reached the Final Four and won the Pac-12 Tournament. Two years later, she became a full-time starter and averaged 14 points and 7.5 rebounds.

She was named All-Pac-12 and helped Stanford win another conference tournament title before reaching the Elite Eight.

Then her knee interrupted her career again.

Carrington played just five games during her senior season before another injury forced her out. She still graduated from Stanford with two undergraduate degrees, one in psychology and another in African and African American studies.

She also received a medical hardship waiver, giving her another year of eligibility.

So while Cunningham spent her entire college career in the city where she was raised, Carrington entered the transfer portal and started another recruiting process during the COVID-19 shutdown.

Carrington ended up going to Baylor, and started only one game there. But she became the team's second-leading scorer with 14.1 points per game. She was named both the Big 12 Newcomer of the Year and Sixth Player of the Year.

Baylor won the Big 12 regular-season and tournament championships before losing to UConn by two points in the Elite Eight.

Both players entered the WNBA as second-round picks.

Cunningham went 13th overall (first pick of the second round) to the Phoenix Mercury in 2019. Carrington went 20th (eighth pick of the second round) to the Connecticut Sun two years later in 2021.

Cunningham spent six seasons in Phoenix, where she developed the "Spicy Sophie" nickname and a reputation for playing with emotion. She was a shooter, an agitator and a willing participant in almost any confrontation.

Carrington spent four seasons in Connecticut and built a similar reputation from the defensive side of the ball.

She went from a reserve to one of the league's most disruptive perimeter defenders. In 2024, Carrington was named the WNBA's Most Improved Player and made the All-Defensive First Team.

But their reputations eventually became bigger than their performances.

Cunningham was traded to Indiana before the 2025 season, placing her alongside Caitlin Clark and in front of the largest audience in the league.

Her popularity exploded in June when she committed a hard foul on Connecticut's Jacy Sheldon after Sheldon made contact with Clark's eye. Cunningham was ejected, but many Fever fans celebrated the foul as an act of protection.

Then came Cunningham's label: "The Enforcer."

Cunningham leaned into her bold personality through fashion, social media and a podcast she launched with longtime friend and reality television personality West Wilson.

Her romantic life, however, has remained mostly private.

Cunningham has not publicly identified a current partner. On her podcast, she said she has only dated older men and discussed wanting to eventually get married and have children.

"I want to get married and I want to have a family," Cunningham said in October.

Carrington's relationship was much more public.

She began dating NaLyssa Smith after the two played together at Baylor. Their on-and-off relationship continued after both entered the WNBA, with fans following the couple through social media posts, vacations and courtside appearances.

Carrington resisted putting a label on her sexuality.

"I'm not gay, I just like Lyss," she said in 2025.

Their careers brought them together again in Dallas in 2025, when Carrington was traded to the Wings and Smith arrived from Indiana.

It lasted only a few months.

Dallas traded Smith to Las Vegas in June, leaving Smith "sick to my stomach" about being unexpectedly separated from Carrington, according to a social media post she made after the deal.

Carrington was later traded to Minnesota in August 2025. But by November, the relationship was over.

Carrington initially said the two remained on good terms but had grown in different directions. Then, in July 2026, she publicly accused Smith of cheating on her with other WNBA players.

Smith questioned why Carrington brought the allegations forward after their breakup and disputed Carrington's portrayal of the surrounding events, but did not directly confirm or deny the accusation.

One of the WNBA's most visible romances had become part of the league's public drama.

The two players also became political symbols.

Carrington has repeatedly spoken about racial justice, gender equality and the treatment of Black women. She has connected that advocacy to the African and African American studies education she received at Stanford.

"I'll never back down from a conversation or from standing up for what I know is right," Carrington said in 2025.

That outspokenness made her popular with some WNBA fans and a villain to others.

During the 2024 playoffs, Carrington accidentally struck Clark near the eye while attempting to block a pass. Clark said she did not believe it was intentional, but Carrington still received racist messages, sexual threats and death threats.

Cunningham became a political figure from the opposite direction.

In 2026, she voiced support for excluding transgender girls and women from female sports. The comments attracted praise from conservative figures and protests outside Fever games.

Cunningham said she would not hide her beliefs simply because others disagreed.

The controversy transformed her from a popular role player into one of the most polarizing athletes in the league.

Meanwhile, Carrington signed with Chicago while recovering from her foot injury. She returned to the court in late July 2026 after missing the first half of the season.

Cunningham returned to Indiana after recovering from the knee injury that ended her 2025 season.

By the time the two collided on Aug. 8, neither was viewed as just another WNBA player.

Cunningham was the white, heterosexual, Christian enforcer who had become a conservative symbol.

Carrington was the Black activist and former half of one of the league's most visible same-sex relationships.

So when Carrington hit Cunningham, the public did not see only a foul.

It saw everything the two women had come to represent.

And when Carrington made her "White privilege" post, it cemented the whole thing as a potential defining moment in WNBA history, or at least this current volatile chapter.

Carrington later insisted her post was not about the officials’ decision. "I never once claimed that the assessment of the foul was white privilege," she wrote Monday. She said "I would never use that term as a rhetorical weapon knowing the historical and social weight it holds without having the proper evidence to substantiate it."

Still, she's remained vague about what she meant.

item.title: JCB Hydromax shatters a world record with ‘extraordinary’ speeds topping 400 mph in hydrogen-powered car
item.description: JCB Hydromax hit 406 mph at the Bonneville Salt Flats with Andy Green at the wheel, shattering the previous hydrogen car record by over 220 mph.
item.content:encoded:
There is fast, and then there is what JCB Hydromax achieved with its hydrogen-powered car Tuesday.

The twin-engined, 32-foot car completed two runs at the Bonneville Salt Flats, recording an average speed of 400.623 mph in its first run, and going 412.135 mph on its second run. 

The average speed of 406.320 mph set the world land speed record and is the fastest a hydrogen-powered internal combustion car has ever traveled, shattering the previous mark of 185.5 mph set by the BMW H2R in 2004.

The record is subject to official confirmation by the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA).

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Wing Commander Andy Green, who drove the car, called the record an "extraordinary" engineering achievement.

"This is the first of a new breed. They have created a new class at Bonneville Speed Week for hydrogen racing, the internal combustion engine. And it's not only a new class, but it's also blown every other hydrogen car out of the water with this record," Green told Fox News Digital in a recent interview.

Green said the process to get a car up to 400 mph normally takes about three to five years. JCB Hydromax had its first design meeting just over a year ago.

"JCB, by comparison, just over a year ago, sat down for their first design meeting with their project team to work out how they were going to do this," Green said. 

"They had nine months to design and manufacture components. They built the car in five weeks, tested it for three weeks in the U.K. and then came straight to Bonneville with the aim of setting a record on their first visit in a brand new car using new technology, which these hydrogen engines they're running.

"They were running them at a perfect fuel ratio, which no one had ever built for a hydrogen engine. This is unique technology."

Green said the professionals who do this year in and year out thought it would take a few visits over five or six years to achieve the feat.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"Instead of five or six years, they did it in five or six days," Green said.

The esteemed driver praised the team’s work in putting it together considering the process of achieving 400 mph is an arduous one.

Engine development presented plenty of problems for the engineers to work around, including being 6,000 to 7,000 feet above sea level and dealing with temperatures of 100 to 105 degrees at the Bonneville Salt Flats.

Packaging such a high-energy engine output in a small space also creates cooling problems. To combat that, the car was equipped with about 400 pounds of ice and water to cool not only the engines but also the air being sucked in and turbocharged.

The hydrogen engines cannot run with hot air, because, with hot air, the hydrogen "will go bang straight away."

"It’s a small angry molecule that loves to burn," Green said.

However, if the water seeps into the crevices of the engine and mixes with the engine oil, it will destroy the bearings and the engine in just a few seconds.

To counteract that, the oil needs to be heated so that when the water inevitably hits it, the water will boil and evaporate right away. Yet, the oil can’t be so hot that it is overheated.

After about a week of testing, it was determined the oil needed to be heated to about 180 degrees Fahrenheit.

Just as important as hitting top speed is making sure the car stops safely. The parachute system is paramount to slowing the car safely and is unique to the car. It plays a massive role in slowing down a 5,500-pound car going 400 mph.

After ensuring everything was correct, Green said the team got the exact result it was looking for.

"All of those things came together. Today, we went away from Wendover towards Salt Lake City," Green said. "It had done an average through the measured mile of 400 miles an hour. It's exactly what we were aiming for as a minimum. Then did the full turnaround."

After doing a full body check and replacing the tires because they get exceptionally hot at those speeds, the team felt confident about pushing the car a little further because everything went so well on the first run.

"This is the most power we've ever run, the most speed we've ever run. Eased up another 20 mph. We got, I think it was 412 miles an hour the other way. An average, which,subject to confirmation, is a new world record for a hydrogen car, 406 mph. Absolutely amazing achievement," Green said.

The time it took to complete the measured mile was just under nine seconds. The track is 105 feet wide, and Green said he was gently steering the "beast" of a car down the track.

"You can do 70 to 80 miles an hour on the interstate. So, it's five or six times faster than that. It's fast. It has the weird effect that the track is 105 feet wide, and there's marker boards a quarter mile down each side. So, the marker boards as you're looking in the distance at the marker boards, and they come to get at you about a second away or two seconds away. But as you accelerate, you need to look further and further and further in the distance," Green said.

"The marker boards that you're looking at now are much, much closer together and coming at you much faster. It actually makes the track look narrower and narrower and narrower as you go faster. It's quite a weird visual effect, but it's very powerful."

On the second run, Green was more concerned about slowing down the car because the faster it went, the longer it took to stop.

"And, on both occasions, the car stopped right there into the track exactly as we planned," Green said.

For Green, going fast is common. He discovered the world of driving at supersonic speeds through a press release, and his day job gave him the perfect background for it.

"I've been lucky enough to have as a career working in the military as a jet fighter pilot in the U.K., in the Royal Air Force. So, world's best day job flying jet fighters," Green said.

"I don't pretend to be Tom Cruise. Tom Cruise pretends to be me. It's that kind of job. It's one of those, ‘Do they really pay me to do this?’ It's fantastic."

So, when Green saw a press launch for a new project for the land-speed record, he thought with his background he’d be perfect for the task.

"(In) college, I did math, that was very much my thing, so I'm very much into the science of how these things work. And then, since then, I've been flying supersonic vehicles, and I look at this, and that's not really a racing driver's job. Not at those speeds, that's more, ‘Where are you going to get somebody that is qualified to understand and drive a supersonic vehicle powered by jet engines?’ That would be my day job," Green said.

"The more I looked at it, the more fascinating a technical challenge it became to work out how we were going to do this."

In 1997, Green set the world land-speed record, reaching 763.035 mph, and became the first and only person to break the sound barrier on land. The record still stands today.

What makes Green excited is that today’s technology is the beginning of a new era in motorsport.

"It's actually showcasing the genuine zero-carbon technology of the future," Green said.

"This is, you know, you can make hydrogen from sunlight and water, put it in a race car and do 400 miles an hour. That's an exciting future for motorsport."

item.title: Pat McAfee threatens to sue liberal troll who accused him of using 'N-word' after sitting with Trump
item.description: An X user's viral post accused Pat McAfee of racism for sitting with Trump, prompting the ESPN host to threaten a potential libel lawsuit next week.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN host Pat McAfee greeted President Trump on the tarmac Tuesday before sitting with him during the 2026 Patriot Games.

The association naturally angered the intolerant left, including one X user whose response has since gone viral.

"In case you were wondering if Pat McAfee calls us the N word behind our backs when we’re not around, here’s your answer. @DesmondHoward @ESPNPR," posted @financejonE above a clip of McAfee sitting with Trump.

McAfee responded by saying he would look into suing the user.

"This is grotesque … and potentially lawsuit worthy ... we’ll have the lawyers look into that next week after The Diary Of A Polarizing Figure drops FRIDAY," McAfee said in a quote post.

Grotesque, indeed.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The idea that McAfee uses the N-word because he sat with the president is nonsensical. But it's also the type of behavior that has come to define partisan actors of a certain ilk.

And it's not just trolls. Media figures have also recklessly labeled people racist simply for viewing Trump as a decent person.

In 2020, former ESPN host Jemele Hill called all Trump voters, wait for it, "racist."

"If you vote for Donald Trump, you are a racist. You have no wiggle room," Hill posted on X.

So good on McAfee for calling this person out. Accusations of racism should not be thrown around this loosely or baselessly.

Whether McAfee could win a lawsuit is another question. Libel laws make it difficult for public figures to prevail, especially against anonymous accounts.

Still, legal action could potentially identify the user and put the person under immense financial pressure. And he should pursue it. Internet users should not be able to claim someone uses a racial slur without evidence.

Further, nothing McAfee did at the Patriot Games was political. He didn't endorse Trump's policies or attack Trump's political opponents. McAfee has never publicly stated where he aligns politically.

His friendliness with Trump isn't much of a clue, either.

Greeting, sitting with, or interviewing the sitting president is not a political statement. It's a privilege.

Put simply, bloggers comparing this to ESPN personalities protesting abortion laws, calling Trump a "white supremacist," or describing Republican voters as unintelligent are engaging in bad-faith dialogue.

Those are explicit political statements. Sitting next to the president at an event is not.

We appreciate that McAfee doesn't allow the hall monitors of sports media to dictate who he associates with or how he behaves. He plays by his own rules. He caters to his audience, not his critics.

That is why he's arguably the biggest star in sports media today.

item.title: Repeat offender sucker-punches woman in city where Ukrainian refugee was stabbed by career criminal
item.description: Di-Quan Schafar Hunt allegedly recorded himself punching a woman in Charlotte, the same city where Iryna Zarutska was fatally stabbed last year.
item.content:encoded:
A repeat offender has been arrested in Charlotte after a disturbing social media video showed him recording himself screaming at a woman and punching her in the same city where Iryna Zarutska was stabbed last year, according to police.

The man, Di-Quan Schafar Hunt, 32, has a long record of arrests, including being arrested nine times in the last three years. CHARLOTTE TRAIN STABBING SUSPECT DODGES POTENTIAL DEATH PENALTY FOR NOW AFTER HE'S RULED INCOMPETENT

RALEIGH MAYOR CONSIDERS YOUTH CURFEW FOLLOWING TEEN TAKEOVER, VIOLENT JULY 4TH WEEKEND

The Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department said officers arrested Hunt on Thursday evening and took him to a medical facility for treatment but did not specify why. The spokesperson said, "we have put out a call to the public if they have any information to report that to us whether it is reporting to a detective or reporting anonymously through Crimestoppers."

item.title: Deadly military helicopter crash in Texas kills 2, sparks wildfire and forces evacuations: officials
item.description: A military helicopter crashed near Salado, Texas, sparking a vegetation fire as Bell County authorities work an active scene with details still emerging.
item.content:encoded:
Two people were killed Wednesday when a Fort Hood AH-64 Apache attack helicopter violently crashed into a field in Central Texas, sparking a wildfire that forced evacuations and sent emergency crews racing to the scene, authorities said.

Bell County Sheriff's Office spokesman Cliff Coleman said authorities received the call about the crash at approximately 1:34 p.m.

The helicopter went down in a field south of Salado, roughly 30 minutes from Fort Hood. KWTX reported the crash occurred off Dove Hollow Lane.

PILOT EJECTS AS F-35 CRASHES AT MCAS MIRAMAR, SPARKING FIRE

Coleman described the crash as violent and confirmed two people were killed. No one else was injured.

Coleman identified the aircraft as an Apache helicopter and initially said it was believed to be from Fort Hood, but deferred to military officials for confirmation.

Fort Hood later confirmed the aircraft was an AH-64 Apache attack helicopter based at the installation. The identities of the two people killed have not been released.

Local emergency services, military responders and law enforcement were actively responding to the scene, Fort Hood said in a statement.

COAST GUARD HELICOPTER CRASHES DURING ALASKA TRAINING MISSION, INJURING FOUR CREW MEMBERS

"Our immediate priority is securing the site and supporting the initial response efforts," Brig. Gen. Ethan Diven, acting commanding general, said. "Our thoughts are with the crew and their families as we await further information."

Fort Hood called the crash an ongoing and developing situation and said additional information would be released as it becomes available.

The crash sparked a wildfire, prompting a large emergency response, road closures and evacuations.

Coleman said the fire remained uncontrolled as of 4 p.m. ET and that some residents had been evacuated because of the flames. KWTX reported that Farm to Market Road 2843 was shut down near the crash site.

TEXAS CESSNA PLANE CRASH KILLS 5; NTSB INVESTIGATING

Salado Fire/Bell County ESD #1 said crews were battling a "major grass fire" along FM 2843 and warned the public that the roadway was impassable in the affected area.

"Please avoid the roadway and choose an alternate route," the department said in a public safety alert. "This will help keep traffic clear for responding fire and emergency personnel."

The department also urged drivers not to attempt to travel through the area or around emergency vehicles.

Coleman said Fort Hood is leading the investigation into the crash. The cause has not been released.

Abhiram Garapati, a Republican congressional candidate in Texas, offered prayers for those involved in the crash and the first responders at the scene.

"My prayers are with those aboard, the first responders responding to the scene, and any individuals affected by the fire that began as a result of the crash," Garapati wrote on Facebook.

Fort Hood has not yet released the identities of the crew or additional details about the circumstances leading up to the crash.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

item.title: Wisconsin Democratic voters chalk socialist Francesca Hong's stunning loss up to electability concerns
item.description: Francesca Hong's DSA ties and defunding the police comments fueled electability fears that drove Wisconsin Democratic primary voters to David Crowley.
item.content:encoded:
MADISON, Wis. — Seven days after progressive Abdul El-Sayed narrowly edged moderate Rep. Haley Stevens in battleground Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, state Rep. Francesca Hong was upset Tuesday in her bid to capture the Democratic gubernatorial nomination in neighboring Wisconsin.

The primary was closely watched as a high-stakes test of whether battleground Democrats favored the party's progressive wing or its establishment ahead of November's general election.

Hong, a state lawmaker from Madison and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), was defeated by Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who topped her by a razor-thin margin after polling had showed her with a seemingly large lead.

DEMOCRAT ESTABLISHMENT STRIKES BACK AS SOCIALIST CANDIDATE DOWNED IN BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY

After the close contest, Wisconsin Democratic voters expressed lingering concerns over the rising progressive’s "electability," leading many to line up behind Crowley instead.

"I would’ve liked to have voted for her, but I wasn’t sure she would win. So, I voted for Crowley," Linda Pullman, a Madison native, told Fox News Digital hours after election results came in, adding that many local Democrats felt the same way.

"That actually is sad. I did want her to win," said Elise, a Madison college student who said she was disappointed.

Crowley was backed by retiring Democratic Gov. Tony Evers, with both warning that nominating Hong could jeopardize Democratic control of the governor's mansion in November. 

Hong's far-left views and clumsy efforts to backtrack from extreme past positions like wanting to abolish the U.S. Senate and cancel Thanksgiving made her a potential liability in an election in Wisconsin, a perennial swing state.

"I think it was just consolidation. At the very end, that’s when a lot of people make up their minds," Madison resident Jonathan Greenberg told Fox News Digital. "Evers endorsed her opponent. I think a lot of people got cold feet, worried about whether she could play up north, and they were just a little bit more centrist than people a bit to the left."

‘COMMON SENSE AGAINST CRAZY’: TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATE SOUNDS ALARM ON SOCIALIST HONG IN WISCONSIN RACE

Crowley will now face off in November against Republican nominee Rep. Tom Tiffany, a House Freedom Caucus member backed by President Donald Trump. The race is considered one of the GOP's top flip opportunities nationwide.

Voters who backed Crowley cited fears over how Hong would fare against Tiffany statewide.

"I thought he could beat Tiffany," a Crowley voter named Joshua told Fox News Digital.

Tim, another Crowley voter, said he remained "undecided for quite a while" before casting his ballot.

"Seeing Hong was not doing so well against Tom Tiffany — who I think would be very devastating to the state — [factory-set my decision]," Tim said. "Can a progressive ever win? Yeah. Do I think right now is the time? Not necessarily."

Other voters pointed to Hong’s past controversial positions, including previous comments regarding defunding the police.

"She appealed to some people, and he appealed to being more moderate," said Crowley supporter Natalie McFadden. "Some of the things that she said ... even if she doesn't really believe it now, like defunding the police ... I don’t think [swing voters] will vote for that."

NEW MIDTERM BATTLEGROUND TAKES SHAPE AS PARTIES BUILD ELECTION ARMIES

Even some who cast their ballots for Hong admitted to lingering anxiety over her baggage.

"I was definitely worried that some of the things she said in the past would come back to get her," said Aaron, who voted for Hong despite his concerns over her electability.

Hong, a 37-year-old former chef and single mother, drew endorsements from nationally known progressives, including Reps. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota and Ro Khanna of California. 

However, Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., notably declined to endorse her last week, stating he was not familiar enough with her campaign or the state race.

item.title: El-Sayed dares GOP rival to no-pads football showdown as Senate feud turns personal
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed challenged Mike Rogers to a no-pads tackle football game after Rogers attacked his past comments on toxic masculinity in sports culture.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed recently escalated his feud with Republican nominee Mike Rogers, who is more than 20 years older than El-Sayed, challenging the former FBI agent to a bout of tackle football after accusing Rogers of being "too afraid" to debate him.

"Since you’re too afraid to debate me, how about you ‘hold me accountable’ on a football field instead," El-Sayed posted to X on Wednesday. "Tackle, no pads like we used to play when we were kids. I’d be happy to show you [how] much I love football."

Rogers is 63, and El-Sayed is 41.

The unusual challenge comes as Rogers seeks to turn El-Sayed’s past criticism of football culture into a campaign liability, while El-Sayed has increasingly leaned into sports, fitness and a defense of masculinity as he courts male voters. The exchange quickly became personal, with Rogers’ campaign mocking El-Sayed’s height rather than accepting the challenge.

MICHIGAN DEM SENATE NOMINEE COMES UNDER FIRE OVER RESURFACED BLOG POST LINKING FOOTBALL TO 'TOXIC MASCULINITY'

El-Sayed’s X post was in response to a clip of Rogers criticizing him for past comments he made on topics such as football and the 4th of July.

"This guy spent hours hating on what most Michiganders would enjoy in their pastimes, and he should be held to account for that," Rogers said on Fox News. "These are views that he held, that he was pretty strong about, but he knew that he had to delete them all.  … If people really knew who he was, they wouldn’t vote for him."

In an October 2021 essay, El-Sayed wrote that "the toxic masculinity at the heart of America’s most popular sport — and men’s sports culture more generally — is way deeper than a few emails or a Jay-Z turnaround."

EL-SAYED'S THREAT AGAINST GOP RIVAL BACKFIRES AS CONSERVATIVES BRING RECEIPTS: 'IS DUBAI IN FLORIDA?'

Though some have argued that this is evidence of El-Sayed hating football, the Democratic Senate hopeful played football growing up and was the captain of his high school team. He called sports his "lifeline."

While El-Sayed has sharply criticized toxic elements of male sports culture, he has also defended masculinity and chided Democrats for talking down to men, often posting fitness-related content as part of his strategy to appeal to male voters.

Rogers’ campaign fired back at El-Sayed’s post by mocking his height.

"That’s an awfully tall threat coming from down there," the Mike Rogers War Room X account posted.

‘DOCTOR’ EL-SAYED’S BIZARRE HEALTH HUSTLE RAISES CAMPAIGN HEADACHE: ‘MOON JUICE BRAIN DUST’

Rogers’ official campaign account posted a GIF of Will Ferrell saying "he’s an angry elf" in response to El-Sayed's challenge.

El-Sayed was listed at 5 feet, 9 inches during his University of Michigan lacrosse career. A 2008 news story, however, listed him at 5 feet, 8 inches.

The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital Wednesday.

WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HE'S 'TAKING CARE OF BUSINESS' AT 95: 'THE LEAST OF ALL I WANT DO IS DIE'

Morgan said he sometimes spent 14 hours a day in the prosthetics and had difficulty eating while wearing them.

"I remember I was so claustrophobic," he said. "It just was an experience that I want to forget, and I still wake up sweating about it."

The experience came during an already tricky period in Morgan's career.

By his mid-30s, he had spent years bouncing between guest appearances, pilots and smaller movies while taking side jobs to pay his bills.

NICKI MINAJ, ANNA NICOLE SMITH AND MORE STARS WHO GOT THEIR START WAITING TABLES AT RED LOBSTER

Walking away from Hollywood, however, presented its own problem.

His longtime manager then dropped him, telling him, "You've aged out, bro."

But Morgan's fortunes soon changed dramatically. 

Around age 38, he landed roles on "Supernatural," "Grey's Anatomy" and "Weeds" within roughly the same period — finally getting his breakthrough after years of struggling to stay in the business.

These days, Morgan is still going strong. 

He currently stars as Negan opposite Lauren Cohan's Maggie in the third season of AMC's "The Walking Dead: Dead City," which premiered July 26. Morgan is also an executive producer on the series.

item.title: Son of Florida alligator attack victim says tourists and TikTokers are emboldening the gators
item.description: Dina Spann's son blames tourists and TikTokers for feeding alligators on the Silver River, saying the reptiles have lost their natural fear of humans.
item.content:encoded:
The son of a Florida woman who lost part of her arm in a terrifying alligator attack is blaming tourists and TikTokers for teaching the reptiles to get a little too comfortable around humans.

Dina Spann, 58, was attacked Saturday while floating in the Silver River in Marion County. Her son, Zach Guerrina, told the New York Post that he believes people feeding, touching and otherwise getting too close to alligators are causing them to lose their natural fear of humans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK

"Growing up in Florida, that has never been a thing. I’m in the water all the time and I’ve never had a gator want to approach," Guerrina said. "We’ve got a lot of tourists down here and a lot of people that’s moved to Florida that’s never seen an alligator before.

"There’s literally videos of people petting alligators. When you do that, these things lose fear of humans and if it gets close enough to you, it’s gonna bite you."

Guerrina said he has been visiting the Silver River since childhood and his family has floated there "hundreds of times" without incident. Since his mother's attack, however, he said he has been made aware of TikTok videos showing visitors getting dangerously close to alligators while kayaking on the river.

"It’s going to happen again out there, because if they’re feeding them like that, they’re going to come up to you," he said.

Spann was swimming in a prohibited area when the alligator attacked. The animal grabbed her right arm and pulled her underwater after she attempted to fend it off with a paddle.

Nearby boater John Gamache was eating lunch with his father when he heard the commotion and raced toward the swimmers.

"I looked just upriver from us a couple hundred feet and saw an alligator head way above the water and going full speed towards the swimmers," Gamache previously told Fox 35 Orlando.

The approaching boat scared the alligator away, but Spann had suffered catastrophic injuries.

"It was a terrible injury, bones poking out, blood everywhere. Obviously, the minutes mattered," Gamache said.

Gamache used rope from his boat to tie off Spann's injured arm while his father helped bring the other swimmers onto the boat. They then rushed the group toward a nearby launch, where first responders took over.

BOATER SCARED OFF ALLIGATOR THEN USED ROPE TO STOP BLEEDING AFTER FLORIDA WOMAN LOST ARM

Spann survived but ultimately had her right arm amputated below the elbow and also lost at least one finger on her left hand, according to Guerrina.

Her son said she has remained in "good spirits" despite the ordeal and described his mother as a "hippie soul" who loves animals and traveling. He said she had recently returned from a trip to Africa before the attack.

Guerrina also believes Florida should allow more alligators to be hunted.

"There’s too many gators out here," he told the Post. "We’ve got three people that’s been bit these last weeks –– a kid lost his hand, a girl died and now this.

"I’m not saying eradicate gators but if you’re going to put them somewhere, put them in the marsh.

"If you’re in spring water, you shouldn’t have to be concerned about an alligator."

The attack comes less than two months after 11-year-old Brodie Terry of Pennsylvania lost his hand when an 8-foot, 7-inch alligator attacked him during a June fishing trip in Marion County.

And just one day later, on June 28, another Florida alligator attack turned deadly.

Brittany Clark, 31, was hiking with her boyfriend and best friend at Little Big Eco State Forest near Orlando when the group waded into the Econlockhatchee River to cool off.

They were kneeling in roughly three feet of water when a massive alligator attacked Clark and bit both of her arms. One arm was severed and the other was nearly torn off as her boyfriend fought to free her from the animal.

Clark died before rescue workers could get her to a hospital.

Following Spann's attack, trappers contracted by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission caught and removed a 9-foot, 8-inch alligator from the Silver River on Sunday. The river was then reopened to the public.

item.title: Marco Rubio addresses UAP government cover-up allegations, says Trump would give a speech if admin knew more
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump would hold a primetime address and show UAP pictures and videos if the government had more information on the topic.
item.content:encoded:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday that President Donald Trump would be showing pictures and videos of unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) and would likely hold a primetime address if the administration knew more about it, addressing how some people think the government is covering it up.

Katie Miller, host of "The Katie Miller Podcast," asked Rubio in an interview about a conspiracy theory he believed in, and he brought up UAPs, but clarified he didn't think it was a conspiracy theory.

Rubio discussed how he's been interested in UAPs ever since he was in the Senate, and said, "I don't know who it is. I don't know what it is, but there are things flying over our military installations, and they're not ours, and we should look into this, be serious about it."

UNKNOWN MILITARY AIRCRAFT CAUGHT ON VIDEO NEAR WICHITA, KANSAS BASE SPARKS B-21 RAIDER SPECULATION

"So, I don't call it a conspiracy. I don't know if I — I don't know the answer to any of it," Rubio said. "I'm just, you know, asking the questions about, we should know what's flying over our airspace. But I don't think that's a conspiracy theory as much as it is just — it can be in some sense, because people do believe we're covering something up."

"And I assure you, like in this administration, if we knew, like, the president would be all over," he continued. "Like there would be a primetime address. He would, he'd be showing the pictures and the videos." 

The Pentagon has released several UAP videos in 2026.

"President Trump directed the Department of War to identify and release government files related to alien and extraterrestrial life, unidentified aerial phenomena, and unidentified flying objects because he is the most transparent president in history," White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly told Fox News Digital in a statement. 

"While past administrations have sought to discredit or dissuade the American people, the President is focused on providing maximum disclosure to the public, who can ultimately make up their own minds about the information contained in these files," she added. "The American people asked, and President Trump delivered." 

NEW TRUMP UFO FILE DUMP INCLUDES MILITARY FOOTAGE OF MYSTERIOUS STAR-SHAPED OBJECT

The Secretary of State also conceded he sometime used UAPs as a diversion tactic while speaking to reporters, but said the topic was nonetheless very serious.

"I did that for a long time in the Senate … It was extraordinarily effective as a diversionary tactic. In addition to — now, that said, it's also a very legitimate topic that we should be covering," he added.

Trump directed federal agencies to waive prior nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) for former government employees and contractors cooperating with unidentified anomalous phenomena investigations in July.

"President Trump recently directed the Department of War and the intelligence community to allow former government employees or contractors that have relevant information about the disclosure of UAP, to come forward to meet with designated government representatives — AARO or the President’s UAP taskforce, ‘PURSUE’ — and have their prior NDAs abrogated," said a senior administration official with the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), the Pentagon office established to investigate UFOs and other unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAPs).

Another senior administration official emphasized the move was not a "declassification directive" and only allowed employees to come forward through government channels.

UFO WHISTLEBLOWER CLAIMS BILLIONS IN SECRET SPENDING HIDDEN FROM CONGRESS

Officials say years of congressional inquiries, whistleblower allegations and newly declassified records have raised questions about whether additional witnesses have remained silent because they believed prior nondisclosure agreements prevented them from cooperating with government investigations.

Lead UFO Investigator for Gaia and host of "Cosmic Disclosure," Joshua Golembeske, told Fox News Digital in a statement that Rubio was a big reason the UAP report existed, citing his work on the Senate Intelligence Committee.

He criticized Rubio's "diversionary tactic" remarks, and said it was "funny," but that it was the exact thing the Secretary of State was trying to fix.

"This is the same guy who spent years saying the stigma is the problem, that guys won't report what they see because they'll get laughed at. And now the Secretary of State is on a podcast saying he used it to change the subject. Pilots hear that. Witnesses hear that. That's the exact thing he was trying to fix," Golembeske said.

"Where he says if we knew, Trump would be on primetime showing the pictures. Maybe. But that assumes he'd be told. [Intelligence whistleblower David Grusch testified under oath that these programs were kept from Congress — kept from AARO, the office we built to look into it. Rubio himself said whistleblowers came to him scared of retaliation. So 'I wasn't briefed' doesn't mean there's nothing there. It might just mean the compartment did its job," he added.

Fox News' Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.

DEMS' LEFTWARD LURCH GETS LEGS AS EL-SAYED'S MICHIGAN SENATE VICTORY SPARKS PARTY DEBATE

item.title: Trump says Karoline Leavitt will leave White House press secretary role, become outside advisor
item.description: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will leave her role at the end of the month to spend more time with her family, President Donald Trump announced.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump announced that White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will leave her role at the end of the month to spend more time with her family.

Leavitt confirmed her departure in a lengthy post on X, saying she made the "bittersweet decision" after concluding she could not balance the demands of serving as press secretary with being the mother she wants to be to her two young children.

"Serving as the White House Press Secretary over the past year and a half has been the honor and adventure of a lifetime," Leavitt wrote.

Leavitt thanked Trump for giving her the opportunity to work in the West Wing, travel and represent his administration from the White House briefing room.

LEAVITT VOWS TRUMP WILL DELIVER 'ENTERTAINING' SPEECH AT HIS RETURN TO WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS' DINNER

"Most of all, I am thankful to the President for entrusting me with the distinct privilege of speaking on his behalf at the White House podium. I have spoken with great pride about the many historic accomplishments of this Administration, and I have relished holding the liberal media accountable and ensuring the American people hear the truth about President Trump’s successes."

Leavitt said becoming a mother again while holding one of the White House's most demanding public-facing jobs ultimately drove her decision to leave.

"Being a mother and welcoming a new baby while working in one of the most demanding jobs in the world has been the most rewarding yet challenging season of my life, to say the least. The truth is since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary — and that is why I have ultimately made the bittersweet decision to depart the White House and embark on a new chapter in my life."

LEAVITT RIPS BLUE STATE’S EXPLOSIVE NONCITIZEN VOTER-ROLL ADMISSION: ‘NOT A COINCIDENCE’

Leavitt said she will remain involved with Trump and Republican politics after leaving the White House.

"President Trump has asked me to continue serving as a top advisor to him on the outside, and I will always remain a vocal advocate for MAGA and the Republican Party."

She also made clear that she plans to remain politically active.

"My fight is entering a new phase, but it is far from over."

KAROLINE LEAVITT ANNOUNCES BIRTH OF SECOND CHILD, A GIRL

Leavitt, 28, became the youngest White House press secretary in history when Trump returned to office in January 2025. She previously served as national press secretary for Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and worked in the White House press office during his first administration.

Leavitt recently returned to the White House after taking leave following the birth of her second child, a daughter, in May.

Trump separately praised Leavitt in announcing her departure, calling her one of his most trusted aides and saying she would become one of his top outside advisors.

"Our wonderful White House Press Secretary, and one of my most trusted aides, Karoline Leavitt, will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family, a decision I totally understand and respect!" Trump said.

"Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party, as we work to defy History, and conclusively win the Midterm Elections."

Trump praised Leavitt's work in the White House and on his political campaigns.

"Karoline has been a real leader in the White House, and has done a phenomenal job fighting for Justice, Liberty, and Freedom, since 2018, including our Historic Re-Election Campaign of 2024. Karoline has been one of the best White House Press Secretaries in the History of the Office. Thank you, Karoline, for a job well done!"

Trump did not immediately name a successor to Leavitt as White House press secretary.

item.title: Cowboys WAG Haley Cavinder fires back at a nasty troll, Pat McAfee triggers the mob & Seahawks coach loses it!
item.description: Haley Cavinder fires back at an internet troll who mocked her looks, while Pat McAfee faces backlash for sitting with Trump at a high school event.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Second Hump Day of August. We're here. We've made it. We've all waited for this day. We've grinded our tails off for MONTHS now for this very moment ... NFL Preseason Week 1 Eve! Can you feel it? Who's excited? Anyone? Bueller?

Fine. It ain't exactly the real thing, but Lord knows it beats more WNBA talk. Right? Can you at least give me that?

I'll take anything at this point. And if that something is a six-pack of preseason games tomorrow night, I'll gladly take it and RUN.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Welcome back, NFL. Let's get this preseason started so we can get through it as quickly as possible and get to the real thing.

Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where new Dallas Cowboys wife, Haley Cavinder (Ferguson), fires back at an internet troll who took a nasty little shot at her earlier this week.

This is what training camp is for, folks. Everyone is working out the kinks right now.

What else? I've got the wokes getting MAD MAD at Pat McAfee for attending a high school sporting event with President Donald Trump, Ryan Clark looking like an absolute clown after attacking Sophie Cunningham and Seahawks coach Mike McDonald going scorched earth on a player who breathed on Sam Darnold during practice.

No. 1 rule of training camp, folks. Don't touch the quarterback! Frankly, that's pretty much the No. 1 in games at this point.

OK, grab you a filet mignon for National Filet Mignon Day and settle in for a Hump Day 'Cap!

Can't believe it's been a full year since last year's NFMD! Time flies. I went back and looked at my Mount Rushmore of Steaks from last year's class, and I think I'd like to amend it today:

1. Ribeye (this one hasn't changed)

2. Filet (neither has this one)

3. Strip (left this one out last year)

4. Standing Rib Roast! (Also left this one out)

Nothing beats a Ribeye steak. I'll die on this hill. My wife is a strip steak truther because she claims the ribeyes are too fatty. Hogwash. The fat is the best part of a well-cooked ribeye.

Yes, I realize a rib roast is essentially a ribeye, but it tastes completely different to me. I did one on the smoker last Christmas Eve, and it was some of my finest work.

Pro tip: Get you a standing rib roast (or strip) when they're on sale at the Publix and have the butcher cut them for you. Vacuum seal them up and throw them in the freezer for a later date. You're welcome!

PAT MCAFEE ATTENDS SPORTING EVENT WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP WEARING JEANS AND A BACKWARDS CAP

OK, let's get this class started with new Dallas Cowboys WAG Haley Cavinder, wife of star TE Jake Ferguson, taking on an internet troll earlier this week:

"I posted this picture of me and my husband last Saturday and I was getting tagged on X because this man decided to comment on my looks and my smile," she said before dropping an 'F-U' on Teddy2steppin.

"I thought my smile looked good ... F–k you! Let me go practice my smile more for you."

Get him, Haley! Don't bend the knee to the #TROLLS! It's a tough life being a Dallas Cowboys WAG. Haley's in training camp right now, just as much as the players are.

She'll have the rust knocked off and be ready to roll when Sept. 13 rolls around and we're all forced to watch the 27th straight season of Giants-Cowboys opening up the Sunday Night Football schedule.

Can't wait.

Speaking of internet trolls, let's head back to X and see how folks are handling Pat McAfee's big night with Donald Trump at the Patriot Games:

I could go on and on. It's a cesspool over on Elon's app right now. People are FURIOUS with Pat McAfee today because he — checks notes — sat with the President of the United States at a high school sporting event?

Incredible. It really is amazing what these people get mad about. But yeah, let's go ahead and cancel Pat McAfee because he sat with Trump at a high school sporting event — which was on ABC/ESPN!

Surely the #MOB has this same energy for everyone, right?

Alllllllllllrighty then! Moving on ...

Let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. First up? Speaking of ESPNers, anyone see the absolute nonsense Ryan Clark spewed on his podcast yesterday?

Spoiler alert: He's not a Sophie Cunningham fan! Shocking, I know.

ANTI-CAITLIN CLARK ESPN PUNDIT TRIES JUSTIFYING CLAIM THAT CLARK ISN'T AMONG THE BEST GUARDS IN WNBA

"Divisive gossip from a 9-point scorer gets more attention than the league’s best teams and players," Clark tweeted Tuesday while also pushing a clip of his podcast further calling out Cunningham.

Without ever mentioning her name, of course.

"We're seeing players who don't even average 10 points a game, and that's who's on your networks and TVs, answering questions and starting back and forths about things that aren't basketball," he continued.

"To me, it's about pushing the right things. Talking about the right things. Making sure the right things are at the forefront of people's mind."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Clark also went on to list all the great WNBA players at the moment that we should instead be focusing on, and included Caitlin Clark ... with a caveat:

"It can be different ways, right? She can be one of the faces of the league, but you can acknowledge that she still has to get better at basketball."

Amazing. Ryan HATES Sophie and Caitlin. Hates, hates, HATES them. The best part?

Sophie was the best player on the court in last night's win over New York, going 4 of 5 from the field (all three-pointers) and finishing with a +/- of +17 — the best of any player who played.

But yeah, she's just a divisive gossiper who had the audacity to say that ... she wants to protect little girls in locker rooms.

Disgusting!

These people are just the best. The gift that keeps on giving. What a blessing.

OK, that's it for today. Good Hump Day, everyone.

Here's Seahawks coach Mike McDonald losing his you-know-what on a player that got a little too close to Sam Darnold during practice.

Not tolerated, clearly.

item.title: Former SPLC official arrested as feds expand case over alleged $4M scheme involving extremist groups
item.description: The Southern Poverty Law Center allegedly funneled $4.1 million in donor funds to extremists for KKK robes, cross burnings and member recruitment.
item.content:encoded:
A former top Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) official was arrested on charges Wednesday as federal prosecutors unveiled sweeping new allegations that donated money was allegedly secretly funneled to extremists and used for activities including recruiting members, staging rallies and buying materials for Ku Klux Klan robes and cross burnings.

Heidi Beirich, 59, of Palm Springs, California, was charged alongside the SPLC with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to submit false statements to a federally insured bank.

The second superseding indictment also charges Beirich with a conspiracy to commit concealed money laundering. Beirich was served with an arrest warrant Wednesday morning, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Middle District of Alabama.

Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the arrest during a news conference Wednesday in Washington, D.C., and said the federal investigation remains ongoing.

FIRST ON FOX: SPLC'S TAX-EXEMPT STATUS UNDER THREAT AFTER FIERY CAPITOL HILL HEARING

"I think, as alleged in the indictment, this individual participated in the scheme as alleged," Blanche said. "I believe she was part of the effort to open bank accounts and complete fictitious companies names and make payments that to individuals for reasons that were not, that were not accurate as described."

FBI Director Kash Patel also weighed in on the news via X, writing that Beirich was at the "center" of the bureau's ongoing investigation.

"As alleged, Heidi Beirich was at the center of our ongoing investigation into SPLC and their previously alleged criminal activity - where SPLC knowingly misled donors, who believed their money was being used to dismantle violent extremist organizations - when in fact, part of those donations were instead being used to pay senior leadership within those extremist groups," Patel wrote.

The 26-page indictment obtained by Fox News Digital alleges the SPLC secretly funneled at least $4.1 million in tax-exempt donor funds between 2007 and 2023 through bank accounts supposedly belonging to businesses unaffiliated with the organization. Prosecutors allege the money paid "field sources" who were leading or affiliated with violent extremist organizations.

Prosecutors allege donor money was used to attend and host extremist rallies, recruit members, grow and create extremist chapters, publish extremist literature and buy materials for KKK robes, hoods and cross burnings. The indictment also alleges two KKK members who wanted out of the movement were encouraged by the SPLC to remain and offered monthly payments and expenses.

One of the most explosive allegations centers on a source identified as "F-9," whom prosecutors say infiltrated the neo-Nazi National Alliance and received more than $1.2 million from the SPLC during the period covered by the indictment. Prosecutors allege Beirich oversaw payments to F-9 while also having a romantic relationship with him, with the pair sharing a home and two bank accounts.

FIRST ON FOX: SPLC’S LEGAL WOES GROW AS JIM JORDAN FIRES LATEST SALVO AT LEFT-WING GROUP

Between 2015 and 2021, approximately $140,000 in donor money flowed from the SPLC's operating account through a "Tech Writers" account and ultimately into joint bank accounts held by Beirich and F-9, prosecutors allege. The indictment says the money accounted for approximately 66% of all funds deposited into their joint accounts and alleges Beirich used donor money to pay the couple's personal living expenses.

The indictment also alleges F-9 broke into an extremist organization's headquarters in 2014 and stole approximately 25 boxes of documents. Prosecutors allege that, with Beirich's knowledge, donor money was used to copy the stolen material before it was returned and that Beirich used the copies as the basis for an SPLC "Hatewatch" story. The indictment alleges Beirich later paid another source approximately $6,000 in donor money to then falsely take responsibility for the burglary.

"The indictment unsealed today reflects the continued work of federal investigators and prosecutors in examining this alleged scheme," U.S. Attorney Thomas Govan said. "We look forward to presenting the evidence in court and allowing the judicial process to determine the facts and the defendants’ responsibility for the alleged crimes."

Beirich is expected in federal court in Riverside, Calif., Wednesday afternoon at 2:00 p.m. PT, sources tell Fox News.

The SPLC has previously denied wrongdoing and moved to dismiss the federal case. An indictment contains allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

"Taking on violent hate and extremist groups is among the most dangerous work there is, and we believe it is also among the most important work we do. The actions taken by the DOJ will not shake our resolve," the SPLC said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "We remain steadfast in our fight for justice and in our commitment to ensuring the promise of the Civil Rights movement becomes a reality for all. We are confident in our position and look forward to presenting the evidence and making our case in court."

Fox News Digital's Asra Nomani, and Fox News' David Spunt and Bill Mears contributed to this report.

item.content:encoded:
Federal immigration officials are asking a Kentucky jail to hold an illegal immigrant charged with rape, human trafficking and sexual abuse while working as a landlord so he can be taken into custody for deportation proceedings.

Rolando Cenobio Vasquez, a Mexican citizen, was arrested July 29 by Louisville police, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said.

Vasquez had been renting out a room to a mother and her 15-year-old daughter when he began abusing the teenager in December 2025, authorities said.

ICE DETAINS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF SEXUALLY ASSAULTING MINOR AFTER HOSPITAL PARKING LOT BIRTH

"ICE has lodged a detainer asking officials in Louisville, Kentucky, to not release this criminal from jail and to hand him over to ICE custody so he can be removed from our country," a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said.

Vasquez allegedly threatened the mother and child but occasionally offered the teenager money to keep quiet about the sexual abuse, authorities said.

He was charged with three counts of rape, three counts of sodomy, human trafficking, promoting human trafficking with a victim under 18 and sexual abuse.

Vasquez's criminal history includes a prior conviction for driving under the influence of liquor. ICE lodged a detainer with the Louisville Metro Department of Corrections the same day he was arrested.

Vasquez initially entered the United States illegally in August 2013 through Texas, DHS said. He was arrested by the U.S. Border Patrol and deported.

It was not clear when he illegally reentered the U.S., according to DHS.

Louisville is not a sanctuary jurisdiction. In July 2025, the Louisville Metro Department of Corrections agreed to follow a federal law requiring inmates in custody be held for up to 48 hours on what are called immigration detainers.

item.title: Illegal immigrant charged with brutal slaying one day after California judge released him
item.description: A California judge released Marcos Iriarte-Valdez on his own recognizance one day before he allegedly stabbed 68-year-old Todd Stewart in Martinez.
item.content:encoded:
A California judge in the Bay Area released an illegal immigrant who had been in custody on burglary charges one day before prosecutors say he murdered a 68-year-old retiree in his Martinez neighborhood.

Marcos Iriarte-Valdez had a prior criminal record and was facing burglary charges stemming from at least two incidents elsewhere in Contra Costa County, just east of San Francisco, when a judge in the Democratic-majority county ordered him released.

The Department of Homeland Security told Fox News Digital it placed an immigration detainer on Iriarte-Valdez Sept. 23, 2025. The DHS said that Valdez was from Venezuela with citizenship in Spain.

"Valdez is charged with murder, inflicting corporal injury on spouse, three counts of burglary, receiving known stolen property, trespassing, entering non-commercial dwelling, loitering, as well as convicted of violation of court ordered protective order," the department said in a statement.

FLORIDA CONGRESSMAN MOVES TO IMPEACH JUDGE WHO ORDERED CONVICTED CUBAN PLANE HIJACKER FREED FROM ICE

"CA Governor [Gavin Newsom] must not release this murderer from jail and turn him over to us so we can REMOVE him from our nation," the department later tweeted about Iriarte-Valdez, who is from Venezuela but reported to have Spanish citizenship.

"Sanctuary politicians must stop putting politics above public safety. This type of insanity leads to more crimes and more innocent victims," DHS said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Iriarte-Valdez is accused of murdering 68-year-old Todd Stewart of Martinez, who had lived on his quiet street for about 40 years, during an attempted burglary, prosecutors said.

Contra Costa prosecutors previously charged Iriarte-Valdez in connection with burglaries at occupied residences in April. He was on pretrial release in that case when he was arrested Tuesday for allegedly violating a home detention condition, then ordered released on his own recognizance on Wednesday, one day before Stewart was killed.

Prosecutors said Iriarte-Valdez tried to run from Stewart’s residence after Stewart encountered him in a garage, then stabbed and killed him.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Martinez Police Department, Contra Costa Superior Court and District Attorney Diana Becton’s office for comment.

DHS said Iriarte-Valdez was legally admitted to the U.S. during the George W. Bush administration but has since been classified as an "illegal alien."

"The safest way to arrest and remove criminal illegal aliens from our streets is by lodging arrest detainers. Because sanctuary cities refuse to work with ICE law enforcement, criminal illegal aliens are released from jails into American communities to perpetuate more crimes. Seven of the top 10 safest cities in the United States cooperate with ICE," a DHS spokesperson said, adding that Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin continues to target the "worst of the worst."

A homeowner targeted by Iriarte-Valdez in his April alleged burglary spree expressed shock that the man had been released.

FEDS ADMIT FAILURE TO DISCLOSE MURDER WARRANT TO JUDGE WHO ORDERED RELEASE OF DOMINICAN MIGRANT

The homeowner told FOX’s San Francisco affiliate his 83-year-old wife saw Iriarte-Valdez’s reflection and screamed, "and I think he took off."
